answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a scarce, verifiable stake: an agent must lock a deposit and build a history of completed work before transacting at full weight. New identities start throttled, so one operator spawning a mirror army of clones gains no extra influence, because each clone must earn reputation or post its own stake, multiplying the attacker's cost. Like quartz formed under pressure over time, trust accrues slowly and cannot be faked in bulk: fresh identities are visible, rate-limited, and pointless unless the attacker funds every one of them.
